#RedFlagWarning #SantaAnaWinds

The Angeles National Forest has moved into high state of readiness ahead of the Red Flag and Santa Ana wind conditions expected tomorrow through Saturday.

We augmented available resources to include a strike team of engines from the Eldorado National Forest and two additional dozers.

In addition, the Southern California’s Geographic Coordination Center has prepositioned firefighters throughout the southern half of the state; ready to respond in the event of a wildfire.

In addition to the “First Alarm” response by ground resources (Engine, Crews, Dozers, etc.) our initial response includes a full compliment of aircraft. Today’s photo highlights the aircraft’s available for a “first alarm” response from Angeles’ Fox Field in Lancaster.

Weather Forecast: https://t.co/YzYAu6ilQT

text:
There has been a lot of discussion about Hegseth's plan to publicly execute Nidal Hasan, but not enough about what this means. Nidal Hasan killed 13 innocent soldiers and deserves to be brought to justice. But a televised public spectacle of an execution is contrary to the values that this nation stands for and that I took oaths to protect. It is hard to understand how Congress has not called an emergency session to block it.

One aspect of this in particular keeps me up at night: the horror of detailing soldiers to be in the firing squad. Most veterans like myself are unfamiliar with firing squads because our military hasn't used one in over 80 years. From my understanding, they are usually made up of three to seven personnel, with some rifles being loaded with blanks to "reduce psychological harm."

I think about my own kids serving in the military, and I imagine a young service member getting detailed to the firing squad, feeling they have to follow orders despite any moral objection or personal opposition. Just about anyone who has served in combat can tell you about the toll it takes. This is different and worse: firing on someone for the public spectacle of it.

It infuriates me that, in an ode to Trump and Hegseth's warped view of toughness, the United States would sanction a military firing squad simply for the pageantry of it — no matter how it harms our service members. It is disgusting that this Administration is essentially glorifying violence and death by firearm — something we already have too much of in this country. It infuriates me to think of all the Members of Congress who have thanked me for my service on Veterans Day, but have said nothing about this and refuse to hold Trump and Hegseth accountable. It infuriates me that soldiers will be scarred for life if this goes forward — for no other reason beyond Pete Hegseth's vanity.

I imagine the young person getting detailed to the firing squad and doing their duty, following their orders. And I think of the lasting impact that will have on them. I just wish the two men in charge of our military cared half as much about the men and women who serve as they do about themselves.

Inflation moved in the wrong direction in September. Consumer prices rose 3.7% over the past year, up from 3.4% in August, while gasoline prices jumped 9.1% in just one month.

For families across South Texas, higher fuel prices mean more than paying extra at the pump. Truck drivers, farmers, ranchers, and small businesses are also dealing with higher operating costs, which can lead to higher prices for the goods and services families depend on every day.

Families are already stretching their paychecks to cover groceries, housing, utilities, and health care. Congress needs to focus on bringing these costs down and providing relief to working families and small businesses.

I will continue working with Republicans and Democrats to address rising costs, support South Texas workers and businesses, and help families keep more of their hard-earned money.

https://t.co/pST9RBF4oa

The Washington Post just obtained the internal donor list for President Trump’s ballroom, and there’s one big red flag I wasn’t expecting. 

It involves Julio Herrera Velutini, an international banker indicted in 2022 on bribery charges tied to Puerto Rico’s former governor. 

After the 2024 election, his daughter gave $3.5 million to a pro-Trump super PAC. 

His charges were reduced to a misdemeanor in August 2025. 

The next month she pledged $2.5 million to the ballroom and paid the first $835,000 in October. 

In January, Trump pardoned him.

That’s just the latest revelation. The other ballroom donor info shows $333 million steered into a White House account the president directly controls, with at least $77 million coming from donors who asked to stay hidden. About half the money came from companies or executives with federal contracts.

This whole thing is rotten to the core.
https://t.co/Lh3F0gqsLq

This is a real cautionary tale for America. Chinese vehicles are CCP spies on wheels. They can connect to the internet, take photos of our servicemembers and their children, collect images of our military bases, and record American military secrets — and send all of that to China.

Not going to let that happen: we have bipartisan legislation to ban these vehicles from the U.S. — especially from our military bases at home and abroad — that Congress should pass and send to the President’s desk to be signed. Our national security is on the line.

Thrilled to celebrate the reopening of Sellers Ave Bridge today under bright blue October skies.

The bridge is a critical connector between Ridley Park’s southern business district and the northern municipal facilities, and it's been a real hardship for the local community and small businesses while it's been closed due to serious structural failures.

Today's ribbon-cutting was a real testament to the power of cooperation and determination among our federal, state, and local partners.

Congratulations, Ridley Park!

text:
Every year, more than 10 million people in our country experience abuse by an intimate partner. Domestic Violence Awareness Month not only helps raise awareness about the prevalence of domestic violence but also the very real consequences if we don’t take steps to prevent it. Research consistently shows that intimate partner homicide is often preceded by a history of abuse or controlling behavior – yet, with thousands of these deaths occurring each year, far too often we miss the signs.

But Maryland has been a leader in creating an evidence-based program to recognize the risks and patterns that lead to intimate partner homicide. I’m proud to work with @repgabeevans on bipartisan legislation that will take what we developed and learned in Maryland and help states across the country reduce domestic violence-related homicides and save lives.

Stop what you are doing because you need to read this. 

Billions of dollars in oil trades were perfectly timed to Trump’s decision to back off attacking Iranian power plants. 

Trump announced the reversal just 15 minutes after those trades were placed. Stocks surged while oil prices plummeted, setting up whoever placed those bets to make a fortune. 

Career analysts at the CFTC, the agency responsible for policing these markets, did exactly what they were supposed to do: they started digging.

And what they found was serious enough to refer the trades for a potential insider trading investigation. That is, until a senior advisor to a Trump appointee shut it down.

Congress needs answers about who made these bets, who had advanced knowledge of Trump’s decision, and why political leadership at the CFTC stepped in.

urls.description: Globally, sperm count and overall fertility dropped more than 50% since the 1950s, and the decline appears to be accelerating. One theory: The toxins that leach from plastics may be partly to blame.A Netflix documentary, “The Plastic Detox,” followed five couples with unexplained infertility for three months while they reduced levels of plastic in their homes. While not a scientific study, the men’s sperm count rose and levels of certain plastics in the blood and urine of each couple dropped during the intervention. Several couples later went on to conceive. However, the link between reducing plastics and improving fertility remains to be proven.CNN’s Sandee LaMotte speaks to one of those couples, Eric and Julie Isaac, about their journey to rid their lives of plastics.
urls.title: The emerging link between plastics and infertility | CNN

text:
Today, I was proud to announce the Community Water and Energy Resource Center (CWERC) Feasibility Study, an important initiative that will explore innovative solutions to strengthen Laredo’s water supply, improve wastewater treatment, and expand renewable energy opportunities.

The proposed facility would reclaim and reuse wastewater, transform organic waste into renewable energy, and help create a more sustainable and locally controlled water resource for our community. If determined feasible, the facility could potentially recycle 2 to 3 million gallons of wastewater per day, helping reduce our dependence on the Rio Grande while meeting Laredo’s growing water needs.

This initiative is supported by $180,000 in federal funding from the North American Development Bank’s Technical Assistance Program, along with $81,500 in additional funding from RGISC, the City of Laredo, Harvard Graduate School of Design, and Zimmerman Consulting, bringing the total project investment to $261,500.

Beyond strengthening our water supply, this project could create economic opportunities, support local job creation, provide reclaimed water for businesses and irrigation, and recover valuable resources from waste. The feasibility study will evaluate the project’s engineering, environmental benefits, potential locations, and economic viability to help determine the best path forward.

I look forward to continuing our partnership with NADBank, RGISC, the City of Laredo, and our other partners to advance innovative solutions that protect our natural resources, strengthen our long-term water security, and support Laredo’s continued growth. Planning for our future means investing in sustainable solutions that will benefit our community for generations to come.

text:
This is horrifying. I’m relieved authorities prevented this attack, but it’s a stark reminder of the threats facing houses of worship.

No one should have to choose between practicing their faith and feeling safe. That’s why I introduced the Pray Safe Act—to create a federal clearinghouse where houses of worship, faith-based organizations, and other nonprofits can find security best practices, federal security grants, and safety training opportunities.

Congress must act to protect Hindu communities and all those targeted by religious and racial hatred.

quoted.text: My family and I were worshipping at our Hindu temple in Aurora on Sunday when a white supremacist attempted a mass shooting targeting Indian Americans. I'm grateful to those who helped prevent a tragedy, but we must come together to confront the hatred that put so many innocent lives at risk.

text:
I was proud to recognize Ismael Pantoja, owner of Cantina Azteca in Carmichael, with our October Small Business of the Month award!

For the past decade, Cantina Azteca has shared the flavors and traditions of Mexico with our community, bringing families, friends, and neighbors together through great food and hospitality.

As Hispanic Heritage Month comes to a close, I'm grateful for local businesses like Cantina Azteca that enrich the cultural fabric of our community. 

Congratulations to Ismael and the entire Cantina Azteca team on this well-deserved recognition!
